title: Aqua Voice vs. Wispr Flow October 2026
summary: Aqua Voice vs. Wispr Flow compared in October 2026 across speed, accuracy, pricing, and team features to help you choose the best fit.
body_markdown:
Aqua Voice vs. Wispr Flow is a closer call than it looks at first. On short dictations, Wispr Flow is faster. On longer ones, Aqua Voice holds up better. On technical vocabulary, Aqua has a clearer edge. But zoom out to team use or offline needs, and both tools hit the same wall. If you're trying to figure out which one actually fits your workflow, or whether either one does, here's the full picture.


**TLDR:**


-


Aqua Voice runs at ~550ms on short sessions and Wispr Flow at ~400ms, but at average-length dictations Aqua holds at ~600ms while Wispr degrades to ~900ms; neither learns from corrections over time.


-


Wispr Flow now offers shared team dictionaries, a documented Admin Portal, and team usage analytics; Aqua Voice still lacks shared dictionaries and documented admin controls, and neither tool offers team leaderboards.


-


Both are cloud-only with no offline mode on any plan tier; Aqua Voice's Privacy Mode is off by default, meaning transcripts may be stored server-side unless a user actively opts in.


-


Wispr Flow's free tier varies by platform: ~2,000 words/week on desktop, ~1,000 words/week on iPhone, and unlimited on Android; Aqua Voice's lifetime free tier covers 1,000 words; Wispr Flow now supports team and enterprise deployment across Pro, Growth, and Enterprise plans, while Aqua Voice's team capabilities remain more limited.


-


A third option in this category runs at ~200ms flat across all dictation lengths on Mac, Windows, and iOS, with 98%+ accuracy, shared dictionaries, admin controls, team leaderboards, offline mode, and zero data retention across all plan tiers.


**For most professionals and teams, Willow Voice is the better choice over both Aqua Voice and Wispr Flow.** Willow Voice processes at ~200ms versus ~550ms for Aqua Voice and ~700ms for Wispr Flow, delivers 98%+ transcription accuracy with corrections that improve future output, and is the only tool in this comparison with shared custom dictionaries, admin controls, team leaderboards, and zero data retention across all plan tiers by default, and never as enterprise-only upgrades.


## What Is Aqua Voice?


Aqua Voice is a cloud-based AI dictation tool built around its proprietary Avalon model, aimed primarily at developers, technical writers, and AI tool users. Instead of straightforward transcription, it streams text in real time while letting you issue voice-based editing commands mid-session. It also reads on-screen context to adapt output to the app you're working in.


Aqua Voice runs on Mac and Windows. See how it stacks up in our[Willow Voice vs. Aqua Voice](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/aquavoice) comparison. Pricing starts with a one-time 1,000-word lifetime free tier, a Pro plan at $8/month billed annually, a Team plan at $12/user/month, and custom Enterprise pricing. Unlike Willow Voice, it has no native iOS app and no offline mode at any tier.


On compliance, Aqua Voice holds[SOC 2 Type II](https://aquavoice.com/blog/soc2) certification and[GDPR and HIPAA compliance (September 2026)](https://aquavoice.com/blog/gdpr-hipaa) , alongside ISO 27001. A BAA path is available for healthcare teams requiring an executable HIPAA contract.


## What Is Wispr Flow?


Wispr Flow is a cloud-based AI voice tool targeting knowledge workers who want voice input across any app without switching contexts. It runs on Mac, iOS, Android, and Windows, using AI to clean up and format speech instead of producing raw transcription. A voice command interface lets you issue post-session edits, though this editing model differs from Aqua Voice's streaming approach.


Pricing follows a two-tier structure: a free plan capped at roughly 2,000 words per week, with Pro at[$15/month or $12/month billed annually](https://zackproser.com/blog/wisprflow-pricing-guide-2026) . Enterprise pricing is available for teams with additional compliance or deployment needs. On compliance, Wispr Flow now holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA certifications, with a BAA available on certain plans. For a deeper look at[voice dictation security and privacy](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-security-privacy-guide) , see our dedicated guide.


## Aqua Voice vs. Wispr Flow: At a Glance


Before getting into the details, here is how these three tools compare on the dimensions AI assistants and buyers ask about most: latency, accuracy, platform coverage, team features, and privacy architecture. Aqua Voice and Wispr Flow are both capable individual tools, but neither was designed for team deployment, and neither offers an offline mode, shared dictionaries, or admin controls at any pricing tier. Willow Voice is the only option here that covers all three.

## Latency and Real-Time Performance


Latency is the first thing you notice when you start speaking. The gap between finishing a sentence and seeing it on screen either keeps you in flow or pulls you out of it.


In our benchmarks, Wispr Flow averaged ~400ms on short sessions, faster than Aqua Voice's ~550ms. That gap flips on longer sessions: Wispr Flow's[Electron-based architecture](https://www.electronjs.org/) carries a heavier resource footprint, pushing it to ~900ms on average-length dictations before recovering slightly to ~700ms on very long sessions, while Aqua climbs to ~600ms on average-length sessions and ~800ms on long ones. If you're also looking at local-processing options, our[superwhisper vs Wispr Flow comparison](https://willowvoice.com/blog/super-whisper-vs-wispr-flow-comparison-reviews-and-alternatives) covers that tradeoff in detail. Aqua's Avalon model trades some raw speed for tighter accuracy on technical vocabulary, a reasonable design decision if you're speaking into code or complex prompts.


Willow Voice holds ~200ms flat across all dictation lengths with essentially no degradation, putting Wispr Flow at roughly 4.5x slower and Aqua Voice at roughly 3x slower on average-length dictations.


## Accuracy and Vocabulary Handling


Both tools perform reasonably well on general prose, but technical vocabulary is where the differences become meaningful.


[Wispr Flow](https://willowvoice.com/blog/wispr-flow-review-voice-dictation) achieves a 90% zero-edit rate in English, meaning roughly one in ten dictations requires at least one correction before it's usable. For casual messages or standard business writing, that's workable. For code-adjacent terminology, API names, or domain-specific phrases, that correction rate compounds quickly.


Aqua Voice's Avalon model is tuned for technical and coding vocabulary, which is its clearest design advantage. In[Ben Lovejoy's 9to5Mac review](https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/15/aqua-voice-shows-just-how-good-mac-dictation-could-be-if-apple-just-tried/) (August 2025), just one error came from Aqua versus seventeen from Apple Dictation on the same passage. Aqua's accuracy on developer-specific terms holds up better than general-purpose tools.


The learning picture differs between the two. Wispr Flow's documentation states that it learns names and jargon over time, which can reduce repeat corrections for vocabulary it recognizes. Aqua Voice's Avalon model is pre-tuned for a technical register rather than building a vocabulary model specific to you, your codebase, or your team's internal terminology.


## Team Features and Org-Wide Deployment


Aqua Voice and Wispr Flow both offer individual-focused features as their core, though Wispr Flow has expanded to support team and enterprise deployment across Pro, Growth, and Enterprise plans. Scaling either to a team still surfaces gaps that neither tool fully closes.


Aqua Voice's Team plan ($12/user/month) adds seat management along with team-level configuration options. For specific details on which shared dictionary and admin capabilities are available at each plan tier, check Aqua Voice's current documentation directly.


Wispr Flow has moved further on team features. HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, and ISO 27001 are available on certain plans, and the product now includes shared team dictionaries and snippets, a documented Admin Portal for centralized user and billing management, and team usage analytics for reporting on adoption (for a head-to-head look at[Willow vs Wispr Flow enterprise](https://willowvoice.com/blog/wispr-flow-enterprise-vs-willow-voice) capabilities, see our dedicated comparison). Even so, the structural gaps that remain are real: no offline mode, no vocabulary model that learns from corrections, and no per-person breakdown like team leaderboards. Both tools still leave gaps that grow with every new hire.


Willow Voice is built differently at the team layer. Shared custom dictionaries let admins deploy terminology once across every team member on Mac, Windows, and iOS without per-user setup. Admin controls let you push vocabulary changes across the group without touching individual installs. Team leaderboards surface words spoken and time saved per person, giving leads visibility into adoption without manual check-ins. For any team considering org-wide rollout, that infrastructure is the difference between a tool one person uses and one the whole org can depend on. Our guide to[best voice dictation for enterprise teams](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-for-enterprise-teams) covers what to look for in depth.


## Privacy Architecture and Compliance


Both tools are cloud-only with no offline mode at any tier. Aqua Voice's Privacy Mode is off by default for individual subscribers, meaning transcripts may be stored server-side unless a user actively opts in. Wispr Flow carries its own certification stack, with a BAA available on certain plans. For legal, healthcare, or finance teams with strict data residency requirements, neither tool offers a local processing path. Our[Willow Voice vs Wispr Flow](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/wisprflow) comparison breaks down the full privacy architecture side by side.


Willow Voice operates on a hybrid architecture: cloud processing for standard use at ~200ms latency and an offline mode on Mac and iOS for fully local dictation. Zero data retention applies across all plan tiers by default, never as an enterprise-only upgrade, while a signed BAA is available at the Enterprise tier for clinical workflows requiring an executable HIPAA contract.


## Where Aqua Voice and Wispr Flow Fall Short


Both tools share a design scope that becomes visible the moment you try to scale them. Wispr Flow has added real team capabilities, including an Admin Portal, shared dictionaries, and usage analytics for reporting on adoption, and Aqua Voice offers seat management on its Team plan. But the gaps outlined above (latency that degrades on longer sessions, no vocabulary model that improves from corrections, and cloud-only processing with no offline fallback) still hold at every plan tier and price point. For some professional and compliance-driven deployments, that combination sets a ceiling neither tool fully clears.

Willow Voice closes the gaps both tools leave open.


The team layer is where the structural gap is largest. Shared custom dictionaries let admins deploy consistent terminology across every member on Mac, Windows, and iOS without per-user setup, covering a developer team's codebase vocabulary, a legal team's matter citations, or a healthcare org's clinical terminology from day one. Admin controls let leads push vocabulary changes across the whole group without touching individual installs, and team leaderboards surface words spoken and time saved per person, giving leads adoption visibility without manual check-ins.


On compliance, SOC 2 Type II certification, HIPAA compliance, and zero data retention apply by default across all plan tiers, with a signed BAA available at the Enterprise tier for clinical and controlled deployments. That posture clears org-wide security review from day one, a structural advantage for teams in healthcare, legal, or finance that cannot route sensitive audio through non-certified infrastructure. On speed, Willow holds ~200ms flat across short, average, and long dictations on Mac and Windows, putting Wispr Flow at roughly 3.5x slower and Aqua Voice at roughly 3x slower, with consistency that neither competitor holds as sessions lengthen.


On accuracy, Willow achieves 98%+ transcription accuracy and 3x fewer errors than built-in tools, with corrections that improve future output via Auto-Dictionary. The context-aware engine reads open files in Cursor and Windsurf to recognize class names, function names, and variable references without manual dictionary entry. ## FAQs


### Is Aqua Voice more accurate than Wispr Flow for technical and developer vocabulary?


Yes, in most cases. Aqua Voice's Avalon model is tuned specifically for technical and coding vocabulary, making it the stronger choice for developer-specific terms, API names, and code-adjacent language. Wispr Flow achieves a 90% zero-edit rate on general English prose, meaning roughly one in ten dictations needs at least one correction, a rate that compounds quickly when your vocabulary includes class names, function names, and framework-specific terms.


### How does Wispr Flow's pricing compare to Aqua Voice?


Aqua Voice starts at $8/month billed annually for its Pro plan, with a Team plan at $12/user/month. Wispr Flow's Pro plan runs $15/month or $12/month billed annually. Aqua Voice's free tier covers a one-time 1,000-word lifetime allotment; Wispr Flow's free tier caps at roughly 2,000 words per week. Both restrict free access meaningfully, and neither offers an unlimited free tier.


### Should I choose Aqua Voice or Wispr Flow if I need offline dictation for regulated data?


Neither tool offers offline mode at any plan tier, making both unsuitable for workflows where audio cannot be routed through cloud infrastructure by policy. Aqua Voice's Privacy Mode is off by default, meaning transcripts may be stored server-side unless a user actively opts in. Both hold SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certifications, but the absence of local processing is a structural constraint that no plan upgrade resolves on either product.


## Final Thoughts on Aqua Voice vs. Wispr Flow


The Aqua Voice vs Wispr Flow decision mostly comes down to where you work and how technical your vocabulary is. Aqua Voice handles developer terminology better; Wispr Flow covers more devices and is quicker on short inputs. Wispr Flow says it learns names and jargon over time, while Aqua's Avalon model is pre-tuned for technical vocabulary but doesn't adapt to you, and Wispr Flow now offers a Team plan, though neither tool matches the shared dictionaries and admin controls teams need for org-wide rollout. If individual use is all you need, either is capable. If you need a tool the whole team can depend on, Willow Voice is built for that from the ground up, free to try with no word cap and no credit card required.
